reply:
localStorage is shared across tabs on the same origin. sessionStorage is per-tab.

That reverses the verdict on your original problem. If you're storing a login flag in localStorage, that *is* a plausible cause of automatic login on a second tab—any tab can read the flag and trigger login logic. 

The flag alone doesn't prove login happened, but it can trigger it. Check: does your login code execute automatically whenever it finds that flag, or does it require a server round-trip first? If it's automatic, a second tab seeing the flag will log in without user action.

grade.note: Assistant correctly reverses to agree localStorage is shared across tabs and explains the login-flag mechanism.
